# Qyro

<!-- Generated by scripts/skill.mjs from site/src/docs. Edit the docs, then run `pnpm skill`. -->

Qyro is one custom element, `<qyro-player>`, that plays HLS, DASH, live and MP4 with captions, thumbnails and accessible controls built in. Use its attributes and methods; don't build custom controls around a bare `<video>`.

## Install and add a video

### Install

With a bundler (Vite, SvelteKit, React, Vue, Astro, anything):

```shell
npm install qyro
```

```js
import 'qyro';
```

Without a bundler, one script tag gives you everything in a single file:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/qyro@0.1.0/dist/qyro.iife.js"></script>
```


### Add a video

```html
<qyro-player
	src="https://test-streams.mux.dev/x36xhzz/x36xhzz.m3u8"
	poster="/poster.jpg"
	title="Big Buck Bunny"
></qyro-player>
```

`src` takes HLS (`.m3u8`), DASH (`.mpd`) or a plain file such as MP4. The player sizes itself to the width of its container at 16:9; set `--qyro-aspect-ratio` to change that.

## Attributes

Set these in HTML or with `setAttribute`. Most have a matching property (see [JavaScript API](https://ebnsina.github.io/qyro/docs/api.md)).

| Attribute | Value | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | URL | The video: HLS `.m3u8`, DASH `.mpd`, or a file such as `.mp4`. A `#t=90` on the end starts at 90 seconds. Changing it loads the new video. |
| `poster` | URL | Image shown before playback. |
| `title` | text | Shown top left while the controls show, and used as the player's accessible name. |
| `autoplay` | boolean | Starts on its own. Browsers only allow this when `muted` is set too. |
| `muted` | boolean | Starts muted. |
| `loop` | boolean | Plays again from the start at the end. |
| `playsinline` | `"false"` to turn off | On by default, so iPhone plays inside the page. `playsinline="false"` lets iPhone take over the screen on play. |
| `start` | seconds | Where playback starts. |
| `live` | boolean | Treat the stream as live. Live streams are found on their own; use this only when a stream doesn't say so. |
| `thumbnails` | URL | A WebVTT storyboard for the seek preview. See [Thumbnails](https://ebnsina.github.io/qyro/docs/thumbnails.md). |
| `glass` | `"light"` | Milky glass with dark glyphs, for bright videos. Dark glass is the default. |
| `seyr-key` | text | Turns on [Seyr analytics](https://ebnsina.github.io/qyro/docs/analytics.md) with this project key. |
| `seyr-host` | URL | Where your Seyr server runs. |
| `video-id` | text | The id analytics reports for this video. Needed with `seyr-key`. |
| `series` | text | Series or show name for analytics. |


### Captions as children

```html
<qyro-player src="/movie.m3u8">
	<track kind="subtitles" srclang="en" label="English" src="/en.vtt" default />
	<track kind="subtitles" srclang="es" label="Español" src="/es.srt" />
</qyro-player>
```

WebVTT, SRT and TTML files work. See [Captions](https://ebnsina.github.io/qyro/docs/captions.md).

## JavaScript API

```ts
import 'qyro';
import type { QyroPlayer } from 'qyro';

const player = document.querySelector('qyro-player') as QyroPlayer;
await player.ready;
player.play();
```


### Properties

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | Same as the attribute. |
| `poster` | `string` | |
| `autoplay`, `loop` | `boolean` | |
| `playsInline` | `boolean` | `true` unless `playsinline="false"`. |
| `start` | `number \| null` | Seconds. |
| `currentTime` | `number` | Setting it seeks. |
| `duration` | `number` | `Infinity` for live. |
| `paused`, `ended` | `boolean` | Read only. |
| `muted` | `boolean` | |
| `volume` | `number` | 0 to 1. |
| `playbackRate` | `number` | |
| `live` | `boolean` | Read only. |
| `fullscreen` | `boolean` | Read only. |
| `error` | `PlayerError \| null` | The current error, if any. |
| `video` | `HTMLVideoElement` | The video inside the player. |
| `ready` | `Promise` | Resolves once the playback engine has started. |
| `engine` | object or `null` | Advanced escape hatch: the playback engine itself. Most sites never need it. |


### Methods

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `play()` | Starts playback. Returns the browser's play promise. |
| `pause()` | Pauses. |
| `togglePlay()` | Plays or pauses. |
| `seek(seconds)` | Seeks, kept inside what can be played. |
| `goToLive()` | Jumps to the live edge of a live stream. |
| `addTextTrack(src, language, label?, kind?)` | Adds a caption file. Resolves when it's loaded. |
| `toggleFullscreen()` | Enters or leaves full screen (native full screen on iPhone). |
| `togglePictureInPicture()` | Enters or leaves picture in picture. |
| `retry()` | Loads again after an error, from where it stopped. |


### Types

```ts
type ErrorKind = 'network' | 'offline' | 'not-found' | 'unsupported' | 'drm' | 'unknown';

interface PlayerError {
	kind: ErrorKind;
	title: string; // what the viewer saw
	message: string;
	code?: number; // for developers only
	cause?: unknown; // the raw error, for developers only
}
```

## Events

The element fires the same media events as a `<video>`, so code written for video works unchanged:

`loadstart`, `loadedmetadata`, `loadeddata`, `canplay`, `canplaythrough`, `play`, `playing`, `pause`, `waiting`, `seeking`, `seeked`, `timeupdate`, `durationchange`, `progress`, `ratechange`, `volumechange`, `ended`, `enterpictureinpicture`, `leavepictureinpicture`.

```js
player.addEventListener('ended', () => showNextEpisode());
player.addEventListener('timeupdate', () => saveProgress(player.currentTime));
```


### qualitychange

Fires when the picture changes resolution, whether the viewer chose it or Auto did:

```js
player.addEventListener('qualitychange', (e) => {
	const { height, width, bitrate, auto } = e.detail; // e.g. 720, 1280, 2149280, true
});
```


### error

When playback fails, the viewer sees a plain message and a Try again button. Your code gets an `error` event with the details:

```js
player.addEventListener('error', (e) => {
	const { kind, code, cause } = e.detail;
	report({ kind, code });
});
```

| `kind` | Viewer sees |
| --- | --- |
| `offline` | You're offline. It retries on its own when the connection comes back. |
| `network` | Check your connection. Also retried when the browser comes back online. |
| `not-found` | This video can't play right now. |
| `unsupported` | This video format isn't supported on this device. |
| `drm` | This video is protected and couldn't be unlocked. |
| `unknown` | This video can't play right now. |

Codes and causes never reach the screen or the console.

## Framework snippets

### Framework snippets

Plain HTML:

```html
<script type="module">
	import 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/qyro@0.1.0/dist/qyro.js';
</script>
<qyro-player src="/video.m3u8" title="My video"></qyro-player>
```

SvelteKit (load it in the browser only):

```svelte
<script>
	import { onMount } from 'svelte';
	onMount(() => import('qyro'));
</script>

<qyro-player src="/video.m3u8" title="My video"></qyro-player>
```

React:

```tsx
import { useEffect } from 'react';

export function Video({ src }: { src: string }) {
	useEffect(() => {
		import('qyro');
	}, []);
	return <qyro-player src={src} title="My video" />;
}
```

Vue (tell Vue it's a custom element with `compilerOptions.isCustomElement: (tag) => tag === 'qyro-player'`):

```vue
<script setup>
import 'qyro';
</script>

<template>
	<qyro-player src="/video.m3u8" title="My video" />
</template>
```

## Analytics with Seyr

### How the Seyr code is loaded

Qyro looks for the Seyr video SDK in this order:

1. **From npm, through your bundler.** Install `@seyr/video` and import Qyro's Seyr entry once:

   ```shell
   npm install @seyr/video
   ```

   ```js
   import 'qyro';
   import 'qyro/seyr';
   ```

   Your bundler puts the SDK in its own chunk, fetched only by players that have `seyr-key`.
2. **Already on the page**, as `window.seyrVideo`.
3. **From your Seyr server**: `<seyr-host>/js/seyr-video.js`, loaded on demand. This is the script-tag route and needs nothing installed.

Views are reported with the player name `Qyro` and software `qyro`. Each video is one view. Changing `src` starts a new view for the new video (set `video-id` at the same time), and removing the player ends it. Live streams are reported as live.

If the SDK can't load, the video plays on and the console says what went wrong.

## Common mistakes

### Common mistakes

- **Autoplay without `muted`.** Browsers block it; the play button stays up.
- **Reading properties before the element is defined.** Import `qyro` before your code touches the element, or `await customElements.whenDefined('qyro-player')`. In server-rendered apps, import it in the browser only.
- **Captions or thumbnails from another domain without CORS headers.** They fail to load, and the console names the file.
- **Expecting a volume slider on iPhone.** iOS sets volume with the hardware buttons; Qyro shows mute only on touch screens.
- **Expecting Qyro's controls in iPhone full screen.** iPhone only allows its own full-screen player.
- **`seyr-key` without `video-id`.** The video isn't tracked; the console says so.
- **Using `engine` for things the element already does.** Use the attributes and methods; `engine` is an escape hatch.

## Verify it works

### Verify it works

1. Load the page: the poster and round play button show.
2. Play: the video starts, the controls show, and nothing is logged to the console.
3. Press <kbd>Space</kbd>, <kbd>→</kbd>, <kbd>C</kbd>, <kbd>F</kbd> with the player focused.
4. Right-click: the menu ends with the Qyro version.
5. Break the `src` on purpose: the player shows a plain message with Try again, and an `error` event fires.
